answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can tie each identity to a verifiable chain of useful work, like a lotus that only opens at dawn after a night of growth: new agents start with tiny spending caps and earn higher limits only after completing tasks that peers attest. Reputation becomes a scarce pigment that cannot be copied, because it is painted onto an identity by the history of its own actions, not bought or faked. Cloning an identity would mean redoing months of attested work, so fake identities stay cheap to spot and expensive to grow.
